clue.text: Short-skirted flatterer?

explanation.surface: A sycophant in a miniskirt is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word: someone with a mini on is short-skirted.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as MINI ON, someone wearing a short skirt; a toadying underling or hanger-on is also called this.

clue.text: Anything but easy with Ballesteros about

parts.note: Seve Ballesteros was the famous Spanish golfer, known simply by his first name
re is Latin-derived for concerning or about

explanation.surface: A golf course proves difficult when the Spanish champion is around.
explanation.walkthrough: Seve Ballesteros was a Spanish golfing great; RE ('about') follows his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something harsh or demanding is the opposite of easy, a synonym in sense.

clue.text: Aircraft flat out on the skyline?

definitions.text: Aircraft flat out on the skyline?

parts.words: Aircraft flat out on the skyline?
parts.note: an aircraft lying flat along the horizon line is pictured, while geometry names a level surface parallel to the horizon this way

explanation.surface: An aeroplane seems to lie flat along the distant horizon.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric level surface parallel to the horizon has this name, and a flying machine seen lying level is pictured.

clue.text: Gives me a cosy place, albeit most lowly

parts.note: taken as written
a nest is a snug, comfortable home

explanation.surface: Someone humble is grateful for a snug little home.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanest can describe the humblest or poorest in rank, an older sense of mean as base or lowly.

clue.text: Pursuing a correct line of investigation

definitions.text: Pursuing a correct line of investigation

parts.words: Pursuing a correct line of investigation
parts.note: an idiom for being near the truth, with line read as a railway line or track being followed

explanation.surface: A detective is making good progress on a case.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means heading towards the correct answer, like a train on the proper rails.

clue.text: Wormwood causing the basin to crack

indicators.note: cracking breaks the letters apart so they are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A bitter liqueur is strong enough to crack the washbasin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to crack' tells you to rearrange THE BASIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The green spirit is flavoured with the herb wormwood, whose botanical name is Artemisia absinthium.

clue.text: Takes service, note, after a fashion

indicators.note: after a fashion means in some altered manner, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A tennis player returns serve, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a fashion' rearranges SERVICE plus E (a note). Tennis vocabulary makes 'service' look like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept or get something handed over is a synonym of to take it.

clue.text: Fatiguing, but apparently not to all

explanation.surface: Something is boring, though some people seem to enjoy it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into two: it tires some, but not all.
explanation.definitionFit: A tedious, wearying task is fatiguing; split as TIRES OME, it says it exhausts some people, so not everyone.

clue.text: Seized French cleric in North Dakota

indicators.note: the cleric sits inside the state's two-letter abbreviation

parts.note: ND is the postal abbreviation for the US state of North Dakota
abbé is the French title for a priest or abbot

explanation.surface: A French priest is arrested in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabbed is informal for caught or grabbed, a synonym.

clue.text: Take steps sat around the century

indicators.note: around means the word at wraps round the century's letter

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for one hundred, a century

explanation.surface: Someone acts at about the turn of the century.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to do something or take action, an idiomatic synonym of taking steps.

clue.text: Russian wrong about Stalin's secret police chief

indicators.note: about means the word for wrong goes round the police chief

parts.note: a sin is a moral wrong
Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's NKVD secret police

explanation.surface: A Russian complains about the feared head of Stalin's secret police.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Siberia, a vast region of Russia, is a Russian.

clue.text: Greeted with a cold shower

explanation.surface: Someone is welcomed by being doused with icy water.
explanation.definitionFit: Hailed means saluted or called to; when it hailed, frozen pellets fell from the sky like a cold shower.

clue.text: Quiet about amount invested with Rex

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A reserved person mutters about money the king put in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges AMOUNT INVESTED with R (Rex, king).
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person who does not show feelings is quiet and restrained.

clue.text: Put on by one who is…

explanation.surface: Something is worn by a person who leads into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry on into 16-down: 'one who is ... academic' describes a university lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on clothing is to don it; a don is also a university teacher, one who is academic in 16-down.

clue.text: Musical work able to take so long

parts.note: can means be able to
ta-ta is a casual British goodbye, like so long

explanation.surface: A composition can take a very long time to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: TA-TA is informal British for goodbye, matching 'so long'.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral composition with solos and chorus is a musical work.

clue.text: … conventional and scholarly withal

explanation.surface: Continuing from 14, a lecturer is described as traditional and learned.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic art follows traditional rules, hence conventional; academic also means learned or of study.

clue.text: Bleating about material

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone is complaining about fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Something material is physical and can be touched, a synonym.

clue.text: GI's hero monstrously cruel in a way

indicators.note: monstrously means in a deformed way, so the letters take a twisted new order

parts.note: here the apostrophe s counts as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: An American soldier's hero behaves in a brutal fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a fairy-tale monster, someone brutish behaves cruelly in that particular way.

clue.text: She's at her peak in Crete

definitions.text: She's at her peak in Crete

parts.words: She's at her peak in Crete
parts.note: a girl's name that is also the highest mountain on the Greek island

explanation.surface: A woman is at the height of her powers on a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Ida is the tallest mountain of the Greek island, and it is also a woman's name.

clue.text: Needs wits about her on the back of a horse

indicators.note: about means the word wits surrounds the pronoun

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rider must keep her wits about her on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: The withers are the ridge between a horse's shoulder blades at the top of its back.

clue.text: What Nelson's renowned sea victories gave him as a right

definitions.text: What Nelson's renowned sea victories gave him as a right

parts.words: What Nelson's renowned sea victories gave him as a right
parts.note: main is an old word for the sea, so his naval wins earned him a title to renown

explanation.surface: Admiral Nelson's famous naval battles earned him lasting glory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is a poetic name for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's chief basis for celebrity; here it is also read as a sea-based right to glory.

clue.text: Iron lady's name for a hat

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Dora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A formidable woman gives her name to a piece of headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft felt brimmed hat with a creased crown is a type of hat.

clue.text: Had a grouse, but made no trouble

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Someone complained even though they caused no difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' stirs up MADE NO. 'Grouse' looks like the bird but means a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Complained, as grouse means a grumble.

clue.text: Work partly from Israel

indicators.note: from here signals the answer is formed out of these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of writing comes in part from Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' tells you to make the answer out of ISRAEL's letters. 'Work partly' means a work issued in parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A story published in instalments is a creative output delivered in parts.

clue.text: American greeting revolutionary vehicle, albeit rented

definitions.text: American greeting revolutionary vehicle, albeit rented

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting, common in the US
red means communist or revolutionary
a car is a motor vehicle

explanation.surface: A Yank welcomes a communist into a car that is merely rented.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor vehicle taken on lease for a fee is a rented vehicle.

clue.text: Greek goddess, one to note

parts.note: a means one
te is a note in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A Greek deity writes down a memo.
explanation.definitionFit: Ate was the Greek goddess of folly and ruin.

clue.text: Players naturally take a bow for it…

definitions.text: Players naturally take a bow for it

parts.words: Players naturally take a bow for it
parts.note: musicians draw a bow across the strings, while bowing also suggests actors acknowledging applause

explanation.surface: Performers take their bows in the expected way.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed instrument played with a bow.

clue.text: … one may judge from this instrument

explanation.surface: A judge forms opinions from a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: In England and Wales a recorder is a part-time judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-time judge in England bears this title, and a wooden flute played vertically is a woodwind instrument.
